{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A names a concrete payer: small Shopify merchants on a monthly subscription. Its price points are anchored to several sourced, live competitor listings ($12.90–$130/mo). Idea B states outright that it has no defined payer yet, which is the most important gap when the goal is a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "A's demand evidence is three independent merchant Reddit threads, each with a link. It is backed by a sourced accessibility-compliance angle that gives the alt-text half a reason to buy now. B's demand quotes come from social-anxiety communities, which signal interest in practice rather than willingness to pay. One quote is a curated testimonial from a competitor's own marketing page.",
    "A's acquisition channel, Shopify App Store ads, can start at a sourced $5/day and reaches buyers who are already in a purchasing context. B's own sourced numbers ($20–$50 per ASO user, $10k–$18k/month agency fees) are hard to recoup at $8–20/month. The brief itself flags CAC payback as unresolved.",
    "B carries risks that A does not have. A professional community questions the evidence base for pragmatics interventions. The brief also notes regulatory and ethical constraints around health claims, recorded voice data, and possible use by minors. All of these add time and liability for a solo operator.",
    "Both markets are saturated, but A's brief identifies a sourced gap in the strongest free incumbent: Shopify Magic does not handle alt text, images, or bulk editing. That gives A a plausible wedge. B's free incumbents (Noora, SpringSocial, Talkville) are described with no comparable gap beyond a single Reddit complaint about chatbots not giving negative feedback."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's payer and pricing evidence. The brief admits there is no defined payer. The $8–20/month hypothesis is anchored to Yoodli, whose pricing is sourced but which sells to enterprise and Team buyers, a different segment from consumer social-skills practice. The closest consumer comparable, Convo's ~$8 price, is inferred from a single user review because no official pricing page was found. So there is no sourced evidence that any consumer in B's intended niche pays a known price for this.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderately confident. A's case is weakened by free, built-in Shopify Magic covering basic descriptions, heavy saturation (one incumbent has 141 reviews and a Built for Shopify badge), and likely one-time-per-catalog churn. A's demand quotes also show procrastination rather than proven willingness to pay. Still, A has a defined payer, sourced price anchors, a cheap channel inside a buying context, and an identifiable alt-text/bulk wedge. B lacks a payer entirely and adds regulatory and reputational risk, so A is the better 90-day first bet."
}
